mods.name: QuickLock
mods.description: Selective server-side container protection with placement ownership, trust, and private access labels.

releases.notes:
First public alpha of QuickLock, an original server-side container-protection mod for Minecraft Java 26.3.

## Requirements

- Minecraft Java **26.3**
- Java **25**
- Fabric Loader **0.20.1 or newer**
- Fabric API **0.165.0+26.3** (tested version)

Install QuickLock on the server only. Players need no client mod or resource pack. QuickLock adds no network port.

## Included

- Placement-based locking rights: ordinary containers stay public until their placer uses `/lock`.
- Container-specific and owner-wide UUID trust, with independent grants and an explicit admin allowlist.
- Protection for chests/double chests, trapped chests, barrels, all shulker colors, furnaces, blast furnaces, smokers, brewing stands, hoppers, droppers, dispensers, and crafters.
- Trusted double-chest expansion and retained protection when one half is removed by its owner.
- Portable shulker ownership/trust and owner-only pickup, with admin recovery.
- Protection checks for destructive actions, hopper/minecart extraction, copper golems, and the Fabric inventory-transfer adapter.
- Optional private red/green aiming labels through vanilla text-display packets.

Commands: `/lock`, `/unlock`, `/trust`, `/untrust`, `/trust-all`, `/untrust-all`, `/lockinfo`, `/lockhelp`, and `/lockview`.

Automation accepts incoming items. Locked block hoppers may pull from protected storage when both have the same owner. Machine outputs sent into public storage or the world are public; users are responsible for safe routing.

## Downloads

- **`quicklock-0.1.0-alpha.1.jar`** — install this server mod jar in `mods/`, alongside Fabric API.
- `quicklock-0.1.0-alpha.1-sources.jar` — source code for developers; do not install this jar.
- `SHA256SUMS.txt` — SHA-256 checksums for both jars.

[Installation and admin recovery](https://github.com/joseph-kelly1/quicklock/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.1/docs/INSTALLATION.md) · [Commands and automation](https://github.com/joseph-kelly1/quicklock/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.1/README.md) · [Testing checklist](https://github.com/joseph-kelly1/quicklock/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.1/docs/TESTING.md)

## Validation and alpha limits

- 10 policy/persistence unit tests pass.
- All 22 dedicated-server game tests pass, including 21 QuickLock tests and one Fabric framework test, both with and without Lithium 0.26.2+mc26.3.
- Independent server processes verify saved locks, trust, viewer preferences, protected contents, and portable shulker identity.
- The packaged jar starts and stops cleanly using the official Fabric server launcher.
- [GitHub CI passed for the tested source tree](https://github.com/joseph-kelly1/quicklock/actions/runs/40158558497).

**This is an alpha prerelease.** Real vanilla-client rendering and multiplayer acceptance, Universal Graves restoration, full companion-stack compatibility, performance at representative load, and actual DiscoPanel operation remain to be checked. Packet-capture tests do not prove client rendering. A matching Fabric release of the intended Fast Leaf Decay project remains unresolved.

Back up the whole stopped world, player data, and QuickLock data together. QuickLock's separate atomic JSON writes do not make Minecraft's chunk and player saves one transaction. Detectable inconsistent protection data stops the server rather than silently reopening containers. Dropped shulkers retain ordinary damage/despawn behavior. Privileged world editing, arbitrary third-party inventory mutation, removing the mod, and unrelated duplication exploits are outside the protection guarantee.
